readings: In `Products`, compute each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices). Compute an overall baseline by averaging `unit_price` directly over all individual products (ignoring missing prices), so each product counts once and types with more products weigh more. Proceed only if the baseline exists. Keep the types whose average is above this baseline. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types whose average is also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall baseline, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
queries:
WITH type_avg AS (
  SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price
  FROM Products
  GROUP BY production_type_code
  HAVING AVG(unit_price) IS NOT NULL
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS b FROM Products WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
),
kept AS (
  SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price
  FROM type_avg t, baseline b
  WHERE b.b IS NOT NULL AND t.avg_price > b.b
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS mean_kept FROM kept
),
final AS (
  SELECT k.avg_price
  FROM kept k, m
  WHERE k.avg_price > m.mean_kept
)
SELECT AVG(f.avg_price) AS avg_type_price,
       AVG(f.avg_price - b.b) AS avg_above_baseline,
       AVG(f.avg_price - m.mean_kept) AS avg_above_kept_mean
FROM final f, baseline b, m;
